Commentary.Commentary: Windies now lead by 212 when they come out to bat as they HAVEN'T FORCED THE FOLLOW-ON. They are way ahead in this game at the moment and some sensible batting will probably see them bat England out of the match. The visitors, on the other hand, need to do what their opposition's bowlers did to them or one would believe they would not stand a chance in this game. Do join us in a while for the last session.

Not a lot you can write about the England batting. They had no answers to the pace and swing on display. 17 was their highest individual score and only 4 batsman managed to cross the double-digit mark. A sorry display with the bat by them!

9 wickets for 47 runs fell in this session! Roach struck in the first over after the break as he got rid of Burns. England never recovered after that. From 35 for 1 they have been bundled out for 77. It was more of exceptional bowling than poor batting. Roach was the star as he got five. Holder and Joseph also shared 4 between them and Gabriel had the sole wicket of Curran to his name.

An absolute demolition there! The Windies bowlers have just rolled back the years. Fast hostile bowling at its best and they get a huge ovation as they walk off the field. Just like Anderson, who took a fifer this morning, it is Roach who leads them off the field. He raises the ball to acknowledge the applause as he walks into the dressing room.

OUT! ENGLAND HAVE BEEN BOWLED OUT FOR 77. That is the lowest total by any team on this ground. Windies lead by 212 runs and have the option of making England come out to bat again. Coming to this ball, it was bowled just outside off on a good length and it shapes away at the last moment to take the outside edge and go to Holder in at second slip. Joseph picks up his second one to finish off the innings. That will also be TEA on Day 2. Incredible bowling, 9 wickets in the session.
FOUR! Rashid becomes the fourth batsmen to cross double figures. Flicks this full one away over mid-wicket for a boundary.
On the shorter side, Anderson gets right behind the line and defends it well.
James Anderson walks in at number 11.

OUT! No. 9 goes down! An absolute snorter that one. Just too much for Curran. Right on the body of the batsman. Curran takes his eyes off the ball and looks to duck awkwardly, the ball though is too quick and before he gets down, it hits his gloves and lobs towards gully. Hope there runs in and takes it easily. An appeal follows and the umpire raises his finger. Curran starts walking back but he is asked to wait. The umpires want to check if Gabriel is cutting the side crease. He isn't and Curran has to continue his long walk back. No heroics from him and another 17 needed to avoid the follow-on.
Fullish and on off, Curran drives it square on the off side.
Another short ball and once again Curran ducks under it.
Bouncer and on the body of the batsman, Curran ducks under it.
Fuller and on off, driven back to the bowler.

DROPPED OR SHORT? By the reaction of the Windies' players, it seems it has fallen just short. Another away swinger on off, Rashid lunges to defend but the ball takes the outside edge. Goes towards Holder who gets low to take it at second slip but the ball lands just short.
Down the leg side, Rashid misses the flick and the ball goes to the keeper.
On the fuller side, Rashid strokes it to covers.
WOW! Pitches on off and then moves away to square the batsman up as he tries to defend. Gets beaten.
Well left! It is slightly outside off, Rashid covers his off pole and shoulders arms to it.
Shortish again on off, Rashid goes back, opens the face of the bat and then guides it to point.
A ripper to end the over! Lands on off and straightens a lot to beat Curran's outside edge by a whisker. Lovely ball.
Bouncer! It is outside off and SC ducks and lets it go through.
Shortens the length this time and Sam is immediately on the back foot to defend the ball onto the ground.
FOUR! Too full, and Curran times is right back past mid off. Once it crosses the fielder in the ring, there is no stopping that one.
Yorker length ball on middle, Sam pushes it back towards mid on.
Short of a length delivery on off, Curran rides the bounce and defends it onto the ground.
Shannon Gabriel comes back into the attack.
On a back of a length around off, Rashid guides it to point.
Some away movement again from outside off, Rashid shoulders arms to it.
Angles this one into the batter, Rashid works it to mid-wicket.
This time he is pushed onto the back foot, Rashid opens the face and guides it to point.
FOUR! Back-to-back boundaries! This time through the off side, full and outside off, Rashid has a go at it. He manages to get it behind point and into the fence.
FOUR! Stylish flick that! Full and on middle, Rashid uses his wrists and flicks it against the swing and over mid-wicket for a boundary.
Solid back foot punch but straight to the man at mid off.
The tempter way outside off and full, Curran is tempted and goes after it, luckily for him it does not take the outside edge.
Fuller in length and way outside off, Curran throws his bat at it, guilty of going too hard. The ball goes off the inner half towards mid on.
A little too short this time, Curran stands tall and defends it onto the ground.
Fuller this time, Curran is rooted to the crease as he goes for the drive, it goes off the outer half to point.
On the shorter side, Curran goes back and punches it to covers.
Twice in a row Rashid is beaten! In the fifth stump channel. Rashid plays inside the line and the ball whizzes past the outside edge.

PEACH! Unplayable! You just have to hope that does not take the edge! Length delivery angled into the batsman. Pitches and leaves him. Rashid plays the original trajectory but gets beaten by the away movement.
Good short ball on middle, Rashid stands tall and defends it onto the ground.
Another nice delivery! Goes wide of the crease and angles it into the batsman, gets it to shape away late. Rashid tries to defend but it goes off the outer half towards point.
Adil Rashid walks in at number 10, he has 10 FC centuries to his name. England would not mind one here.

OUT! Joseph now has a wicket to his name! Another top, top nut this one and the last recognized batsman for England is out of here. This is in the corridor of uncertainty. Shapes away a touch. Foakes lunges and tries to block but is done in by the movement. It takes the outside edge and Dowrich behind takes a neat catch diving to his right. 29 more needed to avoid the follow-on, 2 wickets in hand.
On the pads, it is clipped through square leg and the batsmen take one.
Clips it with the angle to the man at mid on.
A nice looking back foot punch to the man at point.
Back of a length around off, the batter defends it onto the ground.
Good length outside off, left alone.
Whizzes past the outside edge! The sucker ball that from Foakes, it is full and outside off. Ben looks to drive but ends up playing inside the line and gets beaten.
Hits the length hard, gets it to bounce extra, hits the sticker of Foakes' bat as he tries to defend.
Foakes too is handy and is in decent tough. He now pushes this through cover-point and gets to the other end.

On the shorter side, Curran guides it towards point. The fielder there makes a good diving stop to his left, can't stop a run though. Curran has looked to play his shot since he has come out. We have seen how good he is with the bat, need to get him early here.
On the pads again, it is worked to square leg.
Back of a length on off, Curran defends it onto the ground.

FOUR! No, this is not what Windies need. Joseph needs to continue building the pressure, he cannot give away such loose deliveries. It is short and wide outside off, Curran slaps it through covers and the ball races away.
On the shorter side around off, Foakes pulls it towards wide mid on for a run.
Alzarri Joseph to bowl now.
EDGY FOUR! Welcome runs for England, they will take it any which way. Short and outside off, Curran throws his bat at it, it takes the outside edge and goes over the slip cordon for a boundary.
Well bowled and well played! Another short ball which keeps rising after pitching. Curran does well to get on top of the bounce and keep it out.
Another short one and down the leg side, Curran once again ducks under it.
A loose stroke that! Roach won't mind it. Full and wide outside off, Curran goes after it away from his body but gets beaten.
A bumper to welcome Curran, he ducks under it.

Drinks break. An insane hour of play since Lunch and Windies have broken the back of England's batting as they have picked up 6 wickets for 19 runs. The famed English lower order will have their toughest test surely. Let alone getting a lead now, will the follow-on be avoided with Roach spitting fireballs here? Everything is going on here at Barbados, you surely do not want to miss it. The next batsman in is Sam Curran, he did it against India last year but he has a big role to play with the bat here.

OUT! EDGED AND TAKEN! Another one bites the dust. This time it is the man who has most of the times bailed England out of trouble, Jos Buttler. Fifer for Roach, his 9th in Tests and he is on cloud nine at the moment. Another brute of a delivery this, shortish and on off, it keeps climbing on the batsman. Buttler pokes at it and gets an outside edge to the keeper. Into the bowling all-rounders now. The visitors still need another 41 runs to avoid the follow-on. The way the wickets are falling, even that looks farfetched. Never thought I would be writing this.
On the pads this time and Ben flicks it away off his pads.
A good straight drive back down the ground to this full ball on off stump.
Foakes shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.

Yes, no, yes, no and finally the leg bye is taken. A length ball coming in slightly and Buttler misses his flick and gets hit on the thigh pad. Confusion between the batsmen as they finally complete the leg bye. This is what pressure can do.
Left alone outside off by the batsman.
A length ball outside off, swinging away a bit and Buttler plays it with soft hands towards the gully region.

No hat-trick. A poor hat-trick ball to be honest. He should be making the batsman play but instead bowls it outside off, Foakes makes an easy leave. An excellent over though by Roach. A double-wicket maiden.
Hat-trick ball. Ben Foakes is the batsman.

OUT! In the air... taken! My colleague did mention, bowl short to Moeen Ali on this pacey wicket and he won't last for long and that is exactly what happened. None of us thought he would depart on the very first ball though. Kemar Roach  is amidst a brilliant spell. He has four to his name now and England from 35 for 1 have slipped to 48 for 6. They are in tatters at the moment. Coming to the ball now - it is a fast short delivery, right on the body of Ali. He tries to pull it on the leg side by hopping but the ball takes the top edge and flies down towards fine leg. Joseph in the deep does really well to judge it. He keeps his one eye on where the rope is and takes an excellent catch. A golden duck for Ali and Roach is now on a hat-trick.
Moeen Ali walks in at no. 7 with his team in all sorts of trouble.

OUT! Umpire's call on the Hawk Eye and Stokes will have to walk back. Half of England is back in the dressing room now. Is this even real? Roach has his third and Windies are right on top here. Bowls the previous three balls on a short length and pushes this one to a good length. Stokes is beaten by pace and swing and gets rapped on the back foot. A loud appeal beckons and the umpire thinks a bit before raising his finger. Stokes will review it. The ball goes on to clip the top of leg stump. Hence, could have gone both ways but it is umpire's call and England are in dire straits here. The English supporters have gone quiet.
Stokes has been given out LBW! He has reviewed though. Looks close, could go either way. Big moment in the game.
A back foot defense from within the crease towards the off side by Stokes. Looks for a quick single but it is not available.
Left alone by the lefty as it is well outside off.
Left alone once more, Stokes trusting the Barbados bounce as it goes over the off stump.
Jos takes a couple of paces down the track to defend the ball and prevent it from swinging. Good over.
Peach! An absolute peach from the skip that one. Short of a length ball on off and moves away just enough to beat the outside edge of Buttler's willow.
Almost a similar one to the previous ball but this is hit straight back to the bowler. Holder fields it and shadow practices a throw.
FOUR! A lovely drive from Jos that. Fuller one on off, Buttler clears his front leg and times it superbly past mid off for a boundary.
Goes full on the middle stump, Jos comes ahead and flicks it to mid-wicket.
A good length ball outside off and slightly shaping away, left alone by Buttler.
Another one that is shouldered arms to by Stokes outside off.
Left alone outside off this time by the southpaw.
Hurls this one down at the pads, Stokes fails to connect his attempted glance and the ball goes off the pad to Dowrich who dives and takes it down the leg side.
The batsman chooses to leave the ball outside his off stump once more.
A short of a length ball outside off that is left alone by Ben this time.
A length ball on middle, Stokes stands tall and defends the ball back down the ground.
Wide outside off, Buttler drives this after reaching out for the ball.
Wide outside off, left alone this time by the batsman.
A length ball on middle and straightens a tad bit, Jos defends it with soft hands.
Yorker first up on the off stump line to Buttler, dug out by Jos.
Jos Buttler comes in next, replacing his skipper.

OUT! The big fish is gone too! What a passage of play this is for the hosts. The fast bowlers are turning this game on its head. Joe Root has been caught in front here by his counter-part. A slightly fuller length ball on off and coming in quite a bit, Root is beaten as he plays outside the line and gets rapped on the pads in front of the stumps. A loud appeal and the umpire raises his finger almost immediately. Root goes up to his partner and consults him but then together they decide that it would be a waste of a review so he walks off. Good decision that as the Hawk Eye later shows us that the ball would have gone on to have 3 reds. Windies on fire here and picking 4 seamers doesn't seem such a bad decision now. The visitors still trail by 245 runs and look in a little trouble here.
Length ball on off and coming in with  the angle, Root tries to flick it away but does not get good timing.
A good solid front foot defense from Stokes to end the over.

Beaten this time by the away movement. A length ball just outside off to which Ben is ahead to defend but the ball moves away late and beats the willow by inches. Lovely bowling from Roach and BS is having a tough time here.

Left alone again but it is too close for comfort. A good length ball outside off and it comes in this time, Stokes shoulders arms to see it go just inches above the off pole. Good leave it will have to be said though.
Another leave outside the off stump from Stokes. Roach getting the ball to move both ways here.
Going the other way this time, too wide outside off to make Ben play though.
A good leave from Stokes trusting the bounce of the surface. A length ball outside off and coming in, left alone by the batsman.
Tight line and length once again! Back of a length around off, it is blocked.
On a length and around off, Root prods forward and keeps it out.
Another delivery on the shorter side, Root hops and keeps it down onto the ground.
A little too wide outside off to make the batsman play.
Right off the middle but straight to the fielder! On off, Root lunges and then strokes it to mid off.
Good length and on off, Root goes back and defends it onto the ground.
Bouncer! Stokes evades it by ducking.
Ben Stokes walks in at number 5.

OUT! Played on again! In fact, elbowed on by Bairstow! Roach is on fire here, what ever he ate at Lunch has helped a lot certainly. A scrambled seam delivery from him once more and it moves in a bit after landing. The ball bounces more as well and beats the inside edge and goes on to hit the elbow. Then, it deflects on the bottom of off stump and the bails are off. Brilliant start for Windies whereas Jonny is standing wondering what has happened there! England like so often recently, find themselves three down early on in their innings. The hosts' fans are also elated and they're dancing in the aisles.
FOUR! Goes a little too full this time and Jonny is quick to pounce on that one. Bairstow comes ahead and drives this to the right of mid off for a boundary. Good shot!
Beaten! Good line just outside off and the ball straightens a tad to whiz past the outside edge of Bairstow who was looking to defend it.
Length ball on middle, defended back down the ground with a straight bat.
A short length ball outside off, Bairstow pushes it to the right of point who moves and makes a good diving stop, preventing any runs from being taken.
Goes wide of the crease and angles this one in. It is still outside off, the batsman shoulders arms to it.
Fuller and on off, this one also swings away. Root plays it with an angled bat to covers.
Bends his back on this one as he gets it to bounce a touch extra. Root goes back and guides it to gully.
Drags his length back and bowls it around off, Root defends it onto the ground.

FOUR! Off the mark in style! Full and swinging away around off, Root just leans into it and strokes it through covers for a boundary. He did not look to hit it hard there, just let the ball come to him and then just timed it.
Good length around off, Bairstow tries to defend but it goes off the inner half towards square leg. A run is taken.
Jason Holder to continue from the other end.
Wide outside off stump, Root leaves it alone.
Joe Root, the skipper walks in next.

OUT! Soft, soft dismissal. Rory Burns has played it on here and Windies have a wicket just after Lunch. Around the wicket to the lefty, Roach delivers this one on a length outside off stump and angles it in slightly. Burns was looking to defend it with soft hands but does not present a full straight bat. The ball bounces a bit more as well and hits the top of the willow before bouncing on to go and hit the top of off stump. Looks gutted, it was the first ball he was facing after the break and he has to depart. This should lift Roach as well as his team. Can they snap up a few more quickly?

A length ball just outside off, YJB comes ahead and punches it down the ground. Brathwaite at mid off gets his hand to it but cannot stop it fully. The ball runs towards the fence but he chases it and saves a run for his team.
On the off stump line, Jonny was ahead to defend. The ball runs off the thick inside edge and goes towards square leg. A couple is taken.
Bairstow lets this one go outside off again.
A length ball outside off and straightening later, left alone by Jonny.
The two batsmen, the fielders and the umpires are back out in the middle. All set for the second session, who will do better? Jonny Bairstow to face Kemar Roach.
... Day 2, Session 2 ...

Now what will the two teams look for after the break? England will surely want a partnership to be built so that they can assert their position. The Windies, on the other hand, will need to pick a few quick wickets as this English batting line-up is a long one. Do join us for the afternoon session in a short while.

A shared session one can say! It however was all going well for the English side after they bundled out the Windies under 300. Their openers started off in an assured manner but could not score freely. A few minutes before Lunch, Holder sent Jennings back which sees both the sides head into the break pleased with where the match stands at the moment.

Good delivery to end the session! Goes short this time, Burns looks to leave but the ball gets big on him. He fails to get his hands out in time, the ball hits the handle and then rolls towards gully. Lucky that as it could have lobbed to the fielders in the slip cordon. THAT WILL BE LUNCH ON DAY 2!
Closer to the off pole, Burns defends it.
Another ball way outside off, the batter is not interested in playing at those.
Outside off, the batsman need not play at those.
Back of a length on middle, this one comes in with the angle, JB works it around the corner and takes a run.
Should be the last over before Lunch...
Another good delivery, slightly short and it lands around off, pitches and then leaves the batter. Now due to the length, Bairstow has time to adjust to the movement and he makes a leave.
On the hips this time, YJB works it away to deep fine leg for a single and keeps strike.
The batsman has driven this fuller one on off towards mid off.

FOUR BYES! Poor Shane Dowrich, this will go as a wicket-keeping error whereas in real, he had no chance to reach that ball. It was banged in short by Shannon on middle and leg and the ball moves wildly down the leg side as Bairstow ducked to let it go. Even a full length dive from the keeper couldn't help him reach it.
Solid defense this time from Jonny coming ahead.

Oooh! Good line and length this from Gabriel. Just on top of off stump, Bairstow looks to defend towards the off side but gets a thick outside edge towards gully who misfields. No single is taken though, as the point fielder is quick to reach the ball.

Outside edge but does not carry! A fuller length ball just outside off and straightening a bit. Burns looks to defend with soft hands but gets an edge that falls short of third slip towards his left. A half stop is made but the single cannot be prevented.
Jonny Bairstow walks in at number 3.

OUT! The skipper strikes, he draws first blood here. Jennings who looked nice till now perishes. Very good by Holder, he continues to bowl it on a fuller length, this one is slightly outside off. Keaton once again goes for the drive but with no foot movement. The ball takes a fat outside edge and goes into the hands of Hope at gully. Holder is ecstatic as he provides Windies the breakthrough they desperately wanted before the break. Still a few minutes to go, can they take another?
OHHH! Good length there, this was just behind the driving length, Jennings prods forward and looks to drive but gets beaten as it shapes away a touch.
Outside off, shouldered arms to.
Shortens his length and bowls it on off, blocked.
FOUR! No need to run for those! Jennings is looking really good out there. Jason is guilty of bowling a little too full here, Keaton strokes it through mid off and the ball races away.
Angles this across the batter, Jennings plays inside the line and lets it go to the keeper. Replays show that he was actually beaten there.
Attacks the off stump on the last ball, defended.
Good delivery! Bowls it in the corridor of uncertanity, gets it to straighten. Burns first thinks of playing at it but then pulls his bat out of the way.
Late onto that shot! Full and outside off, drawing Burns into a loose shot. He is late in bringing his bat down and the ball goes to the keeper.
Nicely timed! Does not got the fence but three taken. After two back of a length deliveries, Gabriel goes very full. Jennings though is upto the mark, he strokes it past mid off and takes three.
Another solid looking punch but this time finds the man at point. Batting seems easy right now on this wicket.
FOUR! Excellent shot! Short and outside off, it bounces at a good height for the batsman. Jennings stands tall and then guides it through point. The ball races away.
From around the wicket bowls it on middle, Burns works it with the angle towards mid-wicket. So Windies are managing to keep it tight here.
A little too straight this time, KJ clips it to mid on for a run.
Goes back to bowling in-dippers and attacks the stumps. Kept out.
Angles this one away after bowling two inswingers but it is too wide outside off. Left alone.
Good length again around off, it comes in again, Jennings easily gets behind the line and defends it.
Good length and on middle, hint of movement for Holder. Jennings keeps it out.
Jason Holder now into the attack.
Hits the length hard on off, Burns keeps it out.
A little too straight this time, Jennings tries to flick but misses. It hits his pads and rolls towards square leg. A leg bye taken.
Another short ball on middle, it is once again ducked under.
Change in length by Gabriel, he bangs it short and it has been wided.
Defended off the back foot by the batsman.
On off and it is on a length, it is defended.
Goes back to bowling deliveries he has been bowling so far. Way wide outside off, left alone.

BEAUTY! This is what he should keep bowling, this is the length and line is what I mean. It first angles into the batsman from around the wicket which means the batter has to play at it. It pitches and leaves him, Burns is beaten as he plays inside the line.
2 outside off, one down the leg side and another one outside off. It is once again left alone.
Overcompensates and bowls it way down the leg side. Wasting the new ball here, need to make the batsman play more.
Good length again outside off, Burns makes another leave.
Outside off, the batsman need not play at those.
Now follows the bumper with a very full delivery on the stumps, it is stroked to mid off. No movement for Gabriel whereas Roach is getting some.
A bumper now and it is on the body of the batsman, he ducks under it.
On the shorter side on off, Jennings defends it off the back foot.
This is worked with the angle through mid-wicket by Burns and he gets off the mark.
This is angled into the batter, he tries to flick but misses to get hit high on the pads.
On off, Burns gets right behind the line and keeps it out.

In the air... FOUR! First boundary off the bat but it has come in a fortunate manner. Full and wide outside off, Keaton throws his bat at it, it goes off the outer half uppishly towards the point fielder. He dives full stretch to his left but can't reach it.
Down the leg side, KJ looks to flick but misses. Two good balls and then a poor one. Does not go for runs though.

BEATEN AGAIN! Almost an action replay of the last ball. This time though the length was a touch fuller, once again straightens after pitching around off. Jennings is beaten as he tries to keep it out off the front foot.
Good line! On a length and around off, it straightens a touch. Jennings plays inside the line and gets beaten.
Good length again around off, Jennings tries to defend but it goes off the inner half towards mid-wicket.
Too wide outside off to worry the batsman. It is left alone.
Jennings is away with a nicely judged single! He drops this back of a length ball towards cover-point and retains strike.
Fuller this time around off, no swing on offer for the pacer. KJ lunges and defends it onto the ground.
FOUR LEG BYES! England are underway courtesy extras. On the pads, Jennings looks to flick but misses. It hits his pads and goes down to the fine leg fence.
Extra bounce there! Slightly short and on middle, keeps rising on the batsman. Jennings does well to defend it by taking a hand off the handle.
Hits the bat hard as he lands it on a length, Jennings guides it to point.
Starts off from around the wicket, lands it on a length just outside off, Jennings shoulders arms to it.
Shannon Gabriel to share the new cherry.
Peach! A length delivery outside off and straightens at the last moment to beat the outside edge of Burns who was ahead to defend.
Rory shoulders arms to this one outside off once more.
This one is way outside off and holds its line. Burns wants nothing to do with it.
A well-judged leave by the southpaw once more outside off. Lots of inward movement with the breeze there.
Left alone outside off by the lefty this time.
A fuller length ball on off stump to start off with, Burns comes ahead and defends this one back down the ground.
